ideas.author: George Griffith
ideas.line: Protective clothing with an air supply that lets people survive on the lunar surface.
ideas.name: Breathing Dresses
ideas.profit: no lasting profit

verdict.money_why: Space operators buy suits for their crews, and the few firms that already make such gear supply them since the design can be copied.
verdict.prize_why: A suit that keeps a person alive in vacuum is vital to its wearer but serves only the few who work in space.

ideas.author: George Griffith
ideas.line: A term for the planet where a people or species originated.
ideas.name: Homeworld (Home-World)
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Nothing is sold, so nobody pays and no seller collects.
verdict.prize_why: It is a term for the planet a people came from, not a product.

ideas.author: Harry Gore Bishop
ideas.line: The spot in space where a planet's pull and the Sun's pull on an object balance out.
ideas.name: Neutral (Point)
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Nothing is sold, so nobody pays and no seller collects.
verdict.prize_why: It is a natural thing or place in space, not a product anyone makes or sells.

ideas.author: Aleksandr Bogdanov
ideas.line: A crewed spacecraft whose engines draw their power from nuclear fuel.
ideas.name: Etheroneph
ideas.profit: a monopoly-like profit, kept by the maker

verdict.money_why: Carriers and expedition firms buy ships, and many yards could build them once shown how, so established vehicle builders collect.
verdict.prize_why: A working vessel for travel between worlds would found a transport industry of its own.

ideas.arrival: built in 2006, 105 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: Frank Stockton
ideas.line: A gadget that converts speech in one language into another automatically.
ideas.name: Translatophone
ideas.profit: no lasting profit

verdict.money_why: Travellers, migrants and other ordinary people buy it to use themselves, firms buy it too, and once it works many can offer it, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: Letting any two people talk and read across languages opens up travel, trade and work, which is worth an industry of its own.

ideas.author: Harry Gore Bishop
ideas.line: A chain of radio relay stations linking the planets into one messaging network.
ideas.name: Interplanetary Radiograph Station
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by licence holders

verdict.money_why: Assuming firms and settlers pay by the message, nothing described stops a rival from building its own stations, so the carriers and fleet owners who already hold the home networks where every message starts and ends, and the ships to place and tend stations, collect.
verdict.prize_why: Assuming the planets are settled as in the story, a message link among them carries all their trade and news, an industry of its own.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2010s, about 110 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: E.M. Forster
ideas.line: A flat portable display small enough to hold in one hand.
ideas.name: Cinematophote (Blue Optic Plate)
ideas.profit: a monopoly-like profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: People buy it for themselves, the design can be copied, and the electronics firms with the factories and brands collect.
verdict.prize_why: A flat screen you hold in one hand is the face of nearly every modern personal device, an industry of its own.

ideas.arrival: built in the 2010s, about 110 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: E.M. Forster
ideas.line: Carries sound and moving pictures together so callers can watch one another while talking.
ideas.name: Video Communicator
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by platforms

verdict.money_why: Ordinary people pay for the device and the line, and since many can make the device, the firms that already own the phone networks and handset brands collect.
verdict.prize_why: Seeing the person you are talking to is something most people now use, and it is worth an industry.

ideas.author: L. Frank Baum
ideas.line: A clockwork humanoid that moves and speaks once its springs are wound.
ideas.name: Tik-Tok
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: Showmen and exhibitors are assumed to buy it, and many makers could build clockwork figures, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: The description says what this wound-up man does, which is move and speak, and gives it no work or thought, so it is judged as a figure for show and not as the artificial worker of the stories.

ideas.author: E.M. Forster
ideas.judged: AI models could not judge when it may arrive
ideas.line: One planet-wide automated system that provides food, air, shelter and communication for everyone.
ideas.name: The Machine
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Nobody could be charged for it piece by piece, so governments pay, and it is assumed many building and supply firms that hold public contracts would be needed and would collect.
verdict.prize_why: A single system that gives everyone food, air, shelter and talk meets the basic needs of all of humanity.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1960s, about 60 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: E.M. Forster
ideas.line: Lets doctors see and treat patients remotely over a live connection.
ideas.name: Telemedicine Apparatus
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Hospitals and clinics would buy it, and any firm can link a doctor and a patient over a network, so established health providers and network firms collect.
verdict.prize_why: Seeing a doctor without travelling saves time for a great many patients and lowers the cost of care.

ideas.author: Fred C. Smale
ideas.line: A small aircraft that private individuals fly themselves around in.
ideas.name: Aerocar
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Owners buy it as they buy a car, and once it works many firms could build it, so the vehicle makers that already have factories, dealers and repair networks collect.
verdict.prize_why: A private vehicle that flies its owner over the roads would be an industry of its own, though it mostly replaces trips people already make by car.

ideas.author: Jules Verne
ideas.judged: AI models could not judge when it may arrive
ideas.line: A single vehicle that races at great speed on roads, across water, underwater and through the air.
ideas.name: The Terror
ideas.profit: competed away to users

verdict.money_why: I assume wealthy owners buy it, and once it was built other makers could copy it, so no seller keeps much.
verdict.prize_why: A lone vehicle for road, water and air does each job worse than a craft built for it, so it suits a few buyers who want them all.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1910s, about 10 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: George Griffith
ideas.line: Fleets of aircraft in great numbers used to overwhelm defences on the ground.
ideas.name: Aerial Navies
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Armies buy it with public money, and since rival makers can copy it the established arms suppliers with standing army contracts collect.
verdict.prize_why: Striking an enemy from the air changed how wars are fought and supports a whole industry of warplanes and their arms.

ideas.author: George Griffith
ideas.line: A narrow beam of energy that burns living tissue away from the skeleton.
ideas.name: Death-Ray
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Armies buy it with public money, and since rival makers can copy it the established arms suppliers with standing army contracts collect.
verdict.prize_why: Assuming a soldier carries it, it does much the same job as a gun, so the gain over a gun is modest.

ideas.arrival: built in the 1940s, about 40 years after it was imagined
ideas.author: H.G. Wells
ideas.line: A weapon aimed and fired through hand controls and a remote viewing screen rather than direct sight.
ideas.name: Joystick Controls w/Remote Display
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Armies pay, and the idea is easy to copy, so the arms firms that already build the guns and vehicles fit it and collect.
verdict.prize_why: Aiming and firing through a screen and hand controls keeps the crew under cover, but it is a fitting added to weapons, not a new one.

ideas.author: George Griffith
ideas.line: An artillery piece that chills its explosive charge solid so it survives being fired.
ideas.name: Vandelite Gun
ideas.profit: a fat profit, kept by incumbent firms

verdict.money_why: Armies pay, and such guns are easy to copy, so the arms makers that already hold supply contracts collect.
verdict.prize_why: A cannon that freezes its charge so it survives firing is a modest improvement to artillery armies already have.

ideas.author: H.G. Wells
ideas.line: A vast transparent roof sheltering an entire city from weather.
ideas.name: Glass Dome
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: No citizen could be charged singly for the roof over everyone, so the city pays, and the large construction firms that already win such contracts collect.
verdict.prize_why: Sheltering a whole city from weather is a public work on the scale of an industry.

ideas.author: E.M. Forster
ideas.line: A sealed personal room where every need is delivered by automated services so its occupant never leaves.
ideas.name: Machine Apartment
ideas.profit: not judged (not a technology, not something sold, not physically possible, or unclear)

verdict.money_why: Occupants pay for the room and its services, and no single firm could keep the idea to itself, so the appliance makers, builders and delivery networks that already reach every home would collect.
verdict.prize_why: A room that delivers every need by machine would free its occupant from housework and errands, whatever the story thinks of the life that results.
